I think that's more than reasonable. If you want the focus of the sub to be Voater-generated game reviews, than I don't think anyone would fault you for enforcing that rule. It might be a good idea to codify that as a short and simple rule in the sidebar. /v/gaming is big enough that it needed a handful of rules, so we had to cut down a lot of the fluff and just focus on making the rules as simple and understandable as possible so that people read them.

/v/CoOpGaming, on the other hand, is a very small community and doesn't have any special considerations, so the only rule is spelled out right at the top: "All posts relating to cooperative gaming are welcome!". You'll see I included more fluff, suggestions, and links to other subs in the sidebar after that.

My suggestion is that any hard and fast rules you wish to include should be included briefly right at the top and be as short and clear as possible, so that people read them first. You can always elaborate more on the spirit of the sub from there. The risk is that when rules are too long, people just kind of glaze over them and don't really pay them much attention. All subs require different amounts of rules, definitely, but whatever rules there are usually benefit from being clear, short, and right at the top where people pay attention to them.

For things that you don't want to make a hard and fast rule for, you can consider making a non-enforceable guidline, like in this example:

Welcome to /v/GameReviews, a subverse for video game reviews written by regular Voaters.

Rules:

  1. Reviews must be your own creation

Guidelines:

  1. Please include your review as a discussion post instead of just linking to another site. Discussion posts are easy to read and open the floor to questions from other Voaters.

[Fluff text and text about the spirit of the sub would continue from here]
